intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is a must-do for adrenaline seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Day Hike
experiences.description: Often ranked as one of the world's best single-day hikes, this 19.4 km trail crosses volcanic terrain, emerald crater lakes, and dramatic lava fields on the South Island's doorstep. Stunning panoramic views reward every step.

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike the legendary 53.5 km Milford Track through ancient rainforest, past towering waterfalls including Sutherland Falls, and across the MacKinnon Pass. Widely considered the finest walk in the world, this multi-day trek is unforgettable.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River and choose whether to get fully dunked in the water below. A legendary rite of passage in Queenstown.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the world-class Routeburn Track, winding through pristine beech forests, alpine meadows, and alongside crystal-clear mountain streams. The views from Key Summit and Routeburn Falls are absolutely breathtaking and accessible as a day hike.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Day Hike
experiences.description: Often ranked as one of the world's best single-day hikes, this 19.4 km trail crosses volcanic terrain, emerald crater lakes, and dramatic lava fields on the South Island's doorstep. Stunning panoramic views reward every step.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the world-class Routeburn Track, winding through pristine beech forests, alpine meadows, and alongside crystal-clear mountain streams. The views from Key Summit and Routeburn Falls are absolutely breathtaking and accessible as a day hike.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — nothing scheduled before arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~NZD 2) into Queenstown town centre. Check in at Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a leisurely walk along the Queenstown lakefront promenade on Lake Wakatipu — free and stunning introduction to the area.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Queenstown town centre and the vibrant Earnslaw Wharf area. Grab dinner at a budget spot and get an early night to recover from the flight.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport café
meals.lunch: Pick up a meat pie or sandwich from a Four Square supermarket or New World (~NZD 5–8) near town centre
meals.dinner: Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution) — burgers from ~NZD 14–18. Expect a queue but worth every cent

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency or withdraw NZD at the airport ATM. Purchase an Orbus bus card for cheap local transport. November is late spring in NZ — expect mild to warm days but pack layers for alpine areas.

day_by_day.morning: Early start: hike the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (3–4 hours return, free). Begin at Belfast Terrace trailhead — a steady climb through pine forest rewarding you with 360-degree panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables and Cecil Peak. A perfect acclimatisation hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to the Queenstown Gardens (free entry). Walk the perimeter trail around the peninsula, enjoy the rose gardens and take in views of the lake. Visit the Queenstown i-SITE visitor centre to book upcoming experiences and gather free maps for Routeburn and other hikes.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Steamer Wharf area. Watch the TSS Earnslaw steam ship depart at sunset (free to watch from the wharf). Browse the Queenstown Night Markets if operating (Monday markets sometimes run in peak season — check locally).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — pick up oats, fruit and milk from New World supermarket (~NZD 3–5)
meals.lunch: Pak'nSave or New World deli counter — grab a filled roll and a piece of fruit (~NZD 6–8)
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant — legendary rustic pizza and pasta in a stone cottage, mains ~NZD 18–24. Cosy and budget-friendly

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy shoes for Queenstown Hill. The hike gains ~490m elevation — take water and sunscreen. November days are long (sunset ~9pm), giving plenty of daylight.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a shuttle to the Nevis Bungy by AJ Hackett — the highest bungy jump in New Zealand at 134m, suspended above the Nevis River gorge. Book in advance online for best rates (~NZD 275 with transport from Queenstown). The experience includes a scenic 4WD transfer through the Nevis Valley — right from your accommodation area. Jump in the morning session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Recover with a walk along the Frankton Arm Walkway (free, flat 5km trail along the lake edge). Visit the Queenstown Bay beach area for a swim if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gorge Road area to visit the Queenstown Night Market (Thursday–Sunday) or self-cater. Relax and share stories from the bungy jump.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — porridge with banana and honey before the big jump
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and snacks for the Nevis experience (no food available on-site)
meals.dinner: Vudu Café & Larder — hearty meals ~NZD 18–22, great local ingredients and cosy atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy is the headline splurge of the trip — book well in advance. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. The AJ Hackett shuttle departs from Queenstown town centre so confirm pickup point relative to your Nevis Valley accommodation. This is the biggest budget spend day — save elsewhere.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take the Intercity bus to Glenorchy (45 min from Queenstown, ~NZD 15 each way by shuttle). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hours, free) — flat, easy trail through wetlands with incredible views of the Dart River and Richardson Mountains. This is Lord of the Rings country.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the short Glenorchy Wharf Walk and explore the tiny, charming township of Glenorchy. Optional: walk toward the Paradise area on the Rees Valley Track for 1–2 hours (free) through beech forest with mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by late afternoon. Cook a simple pasta dinner at accommodation to save money after yesterday's big spend.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation before departure
meals.lunch: Glenorchy Café — toasted sandwiches and pies ~NZD 10–14. A Glenorchy institution with great mountain views
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta with pesto and vegetables from supermarket (~NZD 5–7 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Glenorchy is one of NZ's most scenic drives — the road follows Lake Wakatipu with jaw-dropping views. Bring a camera. If you have a car, the drive itself is worth doing slowly. Check shuttle timetables in advance as services can be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Full day on the Routeburn Track Day Hike. Take an early shuttle from Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (~NZD 45–55 return with Tracknet or similar). Begin hiking by 8:00am. Walk to the Routeburn Falls Hut (4 hours one way, 8km) through ancient beech forest, cascading waterfalls and alpine meadows. This section is the most accessible and spectacular part of the world-class Routeburn Track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Routeburn Falls Hut (~1000m elevation) for lunch with views over the Hollyford Valley. Explore the area around the falls and alpine basin. Begin the return hike to the car park — allow 3.5 hours back.
day_by_day.evening: Shuttle returns to Queenstown by 6–7pm. Soak tired legs in a hot shower. Enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast — muesli bars, banana, instant oats before 7am departure
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial trail lunch: sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, cheese and crackers (~NZD 8–10 from supermarket the night before)
meals.dinner: Vudu Larder or self-catered — treat yourself to a proper meal after a big hiking day. Noodle dish or stir-fry at home ~NZD 6

day_by_day.notes: This is a strenuous 16–20km day with 800m+ elevation gain. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud. Wear proper hiking boots, carry rain gear (weather can change rapidly), at least 2L water and sunscreen. Book the shuttle the day before. The Routeburn is one of NZ's Great Walks — this day hike version requires no hut booking.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the Routeburn. Sleep in, do laundry, repack gear and resupply at the supermarket for the coming days. Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market at Earnslaw Park (Saturdays, but check Friday options) or browse local shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free Queenstown Hill loop walk lower section or walk the Kelvin Heights Peninsula road (flat, scenic, free) for light exercise without strain on tired legs. Visit the Queenstown Museum (small entry fee ~NZD 5) to learn about the region's gold rush and Māori history.
day_by_day.evening: Queenstown Night Market at O'Connells Pavilion (runs Thursday–Sunday in season, ~NZD 8–15 per dish). Sample international street food and local produce in a lively outdoor setting.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs on toast at accommodation
meals.lunch: New World supermarket deli or a filled bagel from a local café ~NZD 8–10
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market — try 2–3 different dishes from various stalls. Budget ~NZD 15–20 for a full and varied meal

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day — essential after back-to-back big hiking and bungy days. Use the afternoon to plan logistics for the Wanaka leg and check weather forecasts. Book any remaining activities online.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Intercity bus or a rideshare to Wanaka (~1.5 hours, ~NZD 15–25 by bus). Check in at a budget hostel in Wanaka (Wanaka Bakpaka or Base Wanaka, ~NZD 35–45/night dorm). Walk the Wanaka lakefront and visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — the lone willow tree growing in Lake Wanaka, one of NZ's most photographed spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mount Iron Track (1.5 hours return, free) — a short but rewarding loop with 360-degree views of Lake Wanaka, Lake Hawea, and the Southern Alps. The track winds through schist rock formations unique to Central Otago.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka township — smaller and less touristy than Queenstown. Visit Puzzling World (exterior free, interior ~NZD 16) or just walk around the quirky building for photos.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure from Queenstown
meals.lunch: Kai Whakapai Café on Wanaka lakefront — great sandwiches and cabinet food ~NZD 10–14
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen — generous portions of pasta ~NZD 18–22, popular with locals and budget travellers

day_by_day.notes: Wanaka is a quieter, more relaxed alternative to Queenstown with equally stunning scenery. November is a great time to visit before peak summer crowds. The Mount Iron hike is short enough to do even with tired legs from previous days.

day_by_day.morning: Full day hike: Rob Roy Glacier Track (10km return, 3–4 hours, free). Drive or join a shuttle to the Matukituki Valley West Branch carpark (~45 min from Wanaka). This is one of NZ's most spectacular and accessible glacier hikes — crossing swing bridges over turquoise rivers, climbing through silver beech forest to dramatic views of the Rob Roy Glacier and hanging ice cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the upper valley viewpoints. Watch for avalanches calving off the glacier face — a dramatic and memorable sight. Begin the return hike, arriving back at the carpark by 3–4pm.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka. Soak in a hot shower and enjoy a quiet dinner. Visit the lakefront at sunset — Lake Wanaka at dusk is extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before 7:30am departure — oats, coffee from thermos
meals.lunch: Full packed trail lunch: wraps, hard-boiled eggs, nuts, fruit, energy bars (~NZD 8–10 prepared the night before)
meals.dinner: Self-catered at hostel — cook a big pot of pasta or rice with vegetables and canned tuna (~NZD 6–8)

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy track involves a 240m elevation gain and crosses private farmland — stay on the marked trail. The swing bridges are exciting but safe. River levels can rise quickly after rain — check conditions at the Wanaka i-SITE before departing. A rental car or shuttle is needed as there is no public bus to the trailhead.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the stunning Haast Pass Highway (State Highway 6) toward the West Coast — one of NZ's most dramatic road journeys through UNESCO World Heritage rainforest. Stop at Thunder Creek Falls (a 10-minute walk from the road, free) and Fantail Falls (roadside, free) along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Fox Glacier township (~3 hours from Wanaka). Check in at budget accommodation (Fox Glacier Holiday Park or similar, ~NZD 35–45 dorm/powered site). Walk to the Fox Glacier terminal viewpoint (free, 45-minute return walk from the car park) for views of the glacier snout.
day_by_day.afternoon: After arriving in Fox Glacier, take the Lake Matheson Walk (1.5 hours, free) — one of NZ's most iconic walks through kahikatea forest to the famous 'mirror lake' reflecting Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman. Best in calm conditions — late afternoon light can be magical.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before 8am departure
meals.lunch: Pack food from Wanaka supermarket for the road — eat at a scenic pullout along Haast Pass
meals.dinner: The Hobnail Café, Fox Glacier — hearty meals ~NZD 18–24, the main budget dining option in town

day_by_day.notes: Fill up with petrol in Wanaka — fuel is expensive and scarce on the West Coast. The Haast Pass road is windy and narrow in places — drive carefully. Lake Matheson reflections are best in still morning or evening conditions. November weather on the West Coast can be rainy — pack full waterproofs.

day_by_day.morning: Drive 30 minutes north to Franz Josef Glacier township. Take the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk (3 hours return, free) — a well-formed track through the glacial valley to the glacier viewpoint. The scale of the ice and surrounding rock walls is humbling. Interpretive signs explain the glacier's rapid retreat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward the coast and stop at Lake Mapourika (NZ's largest lake on the West Coast, free). Walk the short Lake Mapourika Track (45 minutes, free) through ancient podocarp forest. Spot native birds including tui, bellbird and fantail.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fox Glacier for the night. Enjoy a quiet evening — the West Coast has remarkably dark skies for stargazing if the weather clears.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — cereal and fruit
meals.lunch: Snacks and sandwiches packed from accommodation — eat at the Franz Josef glacier viewpoint
meals.dinner: Self-catered at holiday park kitchen — cook a hearty meal of rice, beans and vegetables (~NZD 5–7)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier access on foot is now limited to viewpoints only — ice cave and guided glacier walks require helicopter access (~NZD 250+) which is outside the budget scope of this trip. The free valley walks still offer spectacular glacier views. West Coast sandflies are ferocious — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south from Fox Glacier back through Haast and inland toward Queenstown via the Crown Range Road. Stop at Knights Point Lookout (roadside, free) for dramatic Tasman Sea coastal views. Continue to Haast township for a fuel and food stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive through Haast Pass and into Central Otago. Stop at the Blue Pools Walk near Makarora (45 minutes return, free) — brilliant turquoise water in a beech forest setting with swing bridges. Arrive back in Queenstown by 5–6pm.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay accommodation. Unpack, do laundry and enjoy a relaxed final Queenstown evening. Walk the lakefront at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before the long drive
meals.lunch: Packed food eaten at Knights Point or Haast township — Haast has a small café/petrol station
meals.dinner: Queenstown — Rata restaurant happy hour snacks or budget option: Subway or a supermarket rotisserie chicken with salad (~NZD 12–15)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~4.5 hours total). Start by 8am to allow time for stops. The Blue Pools walk is highly recommended — one of the most beautiful short walks in NZ. Check road conditions on the NZ Transport Agency website before departure as the Haast Pass can close in bad weather.

day_by_day.morning: Final big hike: Ben Lomond Track from Queenstown (5–6 hours return, free). Take the Skyline Gondola up (~NZD 32 one way, saves 400m of climbing) or hike the full trail from town. The summit at 1748m offers the most spectacular panoramic view in the Queenstown region — Lake Wakatipu, the Remarkables, Cecil Peak and on clear days, Aoraki/Mount Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and return to Queenstown by 3–4pm. Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park (entry ~NZD 52 — optional, or view the free conservation show at 10am/3pm). Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the Queenstown lakefront beach for a swim and relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Queenstown — celebrate the end of an epic adventure. Splurge slightly on a final memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered hearty breakfast before the big climb — eggs, toast, coffee
meals.lunch: Full packed trail lunch eaten at the Ben Lomond summit if weather permits
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant or The Bunker — treat yourself to a proper farewell dinner ~NZD 28–35 for a main. Well earned after 13 days of adventure

day_by_day.notes: Ben Lomond is the most challenging hike of the trip — 1400m elevation gain from Queenstown, or 1000m from the gondola top station. Only attempt in good weather — the exposed ridge above the saddle can be dangerous in wind or rain. Start early (7–8am) for best summit conditions. This is the last full hiking day — savour it.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Pack bags and check out of accommodation. Take a slow walk along the lakefront one last time. Visit a café for a proper farewell New Zealand flat white coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time: if afternoon flight, visit the Queenstown Museum or browse the Queenstown Arts and Crafts Market (weekends). Purchase any last-minute souvenirs from the Two Dollar Shop or local markets rather than tourist shops for budget-friendly keepsakes.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Queenstown Airport via Orbus public bus (~NZD 2) or taxi. Depart New Zealand with incredible memories of hikes, bungy jumps and the world's most dramatic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: One final flat white and a proper New Zealand bacon and egg pie from a local bakery ~NZD 8–10
meals.lunch: Airport food or pack remaining supermarket snacks for the flight
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Queenstown Airport is small but can get busy. Use any remaining NZD cash at the airport or withdraw only what you need as exchange rates back home are poor. Declare any food items at customs. New Zealand biosecurity is strict — dispose of all fruit, nuts and plant material before the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is a must-do for adrenaline seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike the legendary 53.5 km Milford Track through ancient rainforest, past towering waterfalls including Sutherland Falls, and across the MacKinnon Pass. Widely considered the finest walk in the world, this multi-day trek is unforgettable.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River and choose whether to get fully dunked in the water below. A legendary rite of passage in Queenstown.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the world-class Routeburn Track, winding through pristine beech forests, alpine meadows, and alongside crystal-clear mountain streams. The views from Key Summit and Routeburn Falls are absolutely breathtaking and accessible as a day hike.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport, collect luggage, and transfer to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the Queenstown town centre to get oriented. Browse the Queenstown waterfront along Lake Wakatipu and enjoy the stunning mountain scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant restaurant scene on the main strip. Take a gentle walk along the lakefront at dusk to catch the sunset over the Remarkables mountain range.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport café or a nearby takeaway upon arrival
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — mid-range New Zealand cuisine with locally sourced ingredients, great for a first-night treat (~NZD 50–70 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings (Nevis Bungy, Milford Track, Routeburn) and check weather forecasts for the week ahead. Stock up on any hiking supplies or snacks from Pak'nSave or New World supermarket.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump (23 km from Queenstown, ~30 min drive). Arrive early for a 9:00–10:00 AM jump slot. The iconic 43-metre plunge above the turquoise Kawarau River is the world's first commercial bungy site — a perfect warm-up before the bigger Nevis jump later in the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Queenstown and stop at Gibbston Valley Winery for a cellar door wine tasting and cave tour (~1.5 hrs). Explore the scenic Gibbston wine region, known as the 'Valley of Vines', and enjoy the limestone cave ambiance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Walk along the Queenstown Bay boardwalk and browse the Earnslaw Wharf area. Relax at the accommodation and review gear for upcoming hikes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation or stop at Vudu Café in Queenstown before heading out — great eggs and coffee (~NZD 18–22)
meals.lunch: Gibbston Valley Winery bistro — cheese boards, charcuterie, and light meals paired with local Pinot Noir (~NZD 25–35)
meals.dinner: Fergburger on Shotover Street — legendary Queenstown burger institution, casual and excellent value (~NZD 15–20)

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bungy in advance via AJ Hackett website. Minimum weight 45 kg, maximum 180 kg. The Gibbston Valley cave tour runs hourly — book ahead or walk in. Bring a light jacket as the gorge can be cool in the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day adventure: Nevis Bungy Jump. Transfer departs from Queenstown's AJ Hackett base on Camp Street at approximately 8:30 AM. The 4WD gondola ride into the Nevis Valley gorge is itself a thrilling experience before the 134-metre leap — New Zealand's highest bungy platform.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Head to Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful walk among the rose gardens and giant trees along the lakeside peninsula — a perfect contrast to the morning's intensity.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a well-earned dinner in town. Visit the Skyline Gondola for sunset views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu (~NZD 32 gondola fare) before heading down for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at accommodation or a takeaway muffin and coffee from a Queenstown café before the transfer
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich and snacks from a local bakery the night before — lunch break at the Nevis site or en route back
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill on Beach Street — excellent fresh seafood in a relaxed atmosphere (~NZD 40–55 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nevis Bungy is operated by AJ Hackett. Transfer + jump package is typically NZD 275–320. Wear comfortable, non-restrictive clothing. Ankles must be accessible. The experience takes roughly half a day including transfers. Photos and video packages available for purchase on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (45 km, ~45 min from Queenstown) — a stunningly scenic route along Lake Wakatipu. Explore the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway (1.5 hrs, easy flat walk) through wetlands with incredible views of the Humboldt and Richardson mountain ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Routeburn Track Day Hike from the Routeburn Flats trailhead. Hike through ancient beech forest to Routeburn Falls (4 hrs return, ~8 km). The waterfall hut area offers panoramic views of the Harris Mountains — one of New Zealand's most spectacular alpine landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown along the lake road at golden hour — stop at a viewpoint for photos. Quiet evening at the boutique stay.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at accommodation to fuel the hiking day
meals.lunch: Pack a hearty trail lunch — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and energy bars from the supermarket the evening before
meals.dinner: The Bunker on Cow Lane — cozy, atmospheric Queenstown favourite with great burgers and mains (~NZD 35–45)

day_by_day.notes: Start the Glenorchy drive early to maximise hiking time. Wear proper hiking boots and carry at least 2L of water per person. The Routeburn Track section to Routeburn Falls is well-marked and suitable for fit day hikers. Check DOC (Department of Conservation) website for track conditions before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest and recovery morning. Sleep in slightly, then enjoy a café breakfast in Queenstown. Visit the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (2–3 hrs, moderate hike, 400m elevation gain) for 360-degree panoramic views over the town, lake, and surrounding ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Arrowtown (21 km, ~25 min drive) — a beautifully preserved 1860s gold-rush village. Walk the Arrow River Bridges Trail (1.5 hrs, easy), visit the Lakes District Museum, and browse the boutique shops and galleries on Buckingham Street.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Arrowtown before returning to Queenstown — the village has a charming evening atmosphere with great dining options.

meals.breakfast: Bespoke Kitchen on Rees Street, Queenstown — healthy brunch bowls and excellent coffee (~NZD 20–28)
meals.lunch: Provisions of Arrowtown — artisan sandwiches, cabinet food, and great coffee in a charming heritage setting (~NZD 15–22)
meals.dinner: Saffron Restaurant, Arrowtown — award-winning contemporary New Zealand cuisine in a historic stone building (~NZD 45–60 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Hill walk takes approximately 2.5 hours return. The summit has a distinctive 'basket of dreams' sculpture. Arrowtown's Chinese Settlement (free entry) near the Arrow River is historically fascinating and worth 30 minutes. Parking in Arrowtown is free and plentiful.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early for Te Anau (170 km, ~2 hrs drive). Check in to a pre-booked guesthouse or motel in Te Anau (base for Milford Track). Stop at Kingston and Five Rivers lookout for photos along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Te Anau and explore the lakefront. Take the Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour (2 hrs, NZD 85–95 per person) — a magical underground limestone cave system with a glowworm grotto, accessible only by boat across Lake Te Anau.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Te Anau's peaceful lakefront promenade. Visit the DOC visitor centre to confirm Milford Track logistics and collect any permits. Prepare hiking gear for the next three days.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation in Queenstown before departure
meals.lunch: Stop at a café in Mossburn or Five Rivers on the drive — or pack sandwiches for a scenic roadside picnic
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck Restaurant, Te Anau — popular local favourite with hearty mains including venison and lamb (~NZD 35–50)

day_by_day.notes: Milford Track is a 4-day/3-night Great Walk requiring advance DOC hut bookings (open from late October). Huts cost approximately NZD 70–80 per night. The track runs one-way from Glade Wharf to Sandfly Point. A water taxi from Te Anau Downs to Glade Wharf departs at approximately 2:00 PM daily. Confirm all bookings well in advance — this is one of New Zealand's most popular tracks.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 1: Transfer from Te Anau to Te Anau Downs (30 min bus), then take the water taxi across Lake Te Anau to Glade Wharf (departure ~2:00 PM — morning is free for final preparations). Morning: last-minute gear check, visit Te Anau's outdoor gear shops if needed, and enjoy a relaxed breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Water taxi departs Te Anau Downs at 2:00 PM, arriving Glade Wharf ~2:45 PM. Begin the easy 5 km walk through ancient podocarp forest to Clinton Hut (elevation gain minimal). Arrive at Clinton Hut by late afternoon — capacity 40 bunks.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Clinton Hut, meet fellow hikers, and enjoy the communal atmosphere. The hut warden gives a briefing on the track ahead. Read, relax, and enjoy the forest sounds.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Te Anau — Miles Better Pies or Ristorante Pizzeria 1852 for a big send-off meal (~NZD 18–25)
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from Te Anau supermarket — this is your last chance to buy fresh food before the track
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dinner at Clinton Hut using your packed dehydrated meals or hut kitchen facilities — gas cookers available

day_by_day.notes: Pack all food for 3 nights on the track. Huts have gas cookers, water, and toilets but no electricity. Recommended pack weight: 10–14 kg. Sandflies are prolific on the Milford Track — carry insect repellent. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the alpine sections ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 2: Depart Clinton Hut after breakfast (~8:00 AM). Hike 16.5 km through the Clinton Valley to Mintaro Hut. The trail follows the Clinton River through magnificent beech forest with towering valley walls. Pass Hidden Lake and the stunning Prairie viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through increasingly dramatic scenery as the valley narrows. The final section climbs gently toward the alpine zone near the base of Mackinnon Pass. Arrive at Mintaro Hut (~5–6 hrs total hiking) by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Mintaro Hut with views up toward the pass. The hut warden provides a weather briefing for the Mackinnon Pass crossing tomorrow — the highlight of the entire track. Prepare gear for an early start.

meals.breakfast: Self-cooked porridge or muesli at Clinton Hut
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten on the track — energy bars, cheese, crackers, dried fruit
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dehydrated meal at Mintaro Hut — popular options include freeze-dried pasta or curry

day_by_day.notes: Today's hike is mostly flat to gently undulating — a good warm-up for the challenging Mackinnon Pass crossing tomorrow. Water is safe to drink directly from streams on the track. The Clinton Valley is famous for its clarity and tranquility. Look out for kea (alpine parrots) near the hut.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 3: The iconic Mackinnon Pass crossing. Depart Mintaro Hut early (~7:30 AM). Climb 900m over 4 km to the Mackinnon Pass summit (1,154m) — the highest point of the track with breathtaking 360-degree views of the Fiordland mountains (weather permitting). Visit the Mackinnon Pass memorial shelter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the dramatic western side of the pass through spectacular alpine scenery. Optional detour to Sutherland Falls (580m — one of the world's tallest waterfalls, 30 min return detour — highly recommended). Continue to Dumpling Hut, arriving in the afternoon after approximately 14 km of hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the Mackinnon Pass crossing with fellow hikers at Dumpling Hut. This is typically the most social evening on the track. The hut has a great atmosphere and the sense of achievement is palpable.

meals.breakfast: Hearty self-cooked breakfast at Mintaro Hut — this is the most demanding day, fuel up well
meals.lunch: Hot drinks and snacks at the Mackinnon Pass shelter, plus trail lunch on the descent
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dehydrated meal at Dumpling Hut — treat yourself to a hot chocolate from your supplies

day_by_day.notes: Mackinnon Pass can experience severe weather even in November. If the pass is closed due to weather, the hut warden will advise on safety and potential delays. Carry all wet-weather gear. The Sutherland Falls detour adds ~1 hour but is one of the most spectacular sights on the entire South Island — do not skip it if conditions allow.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 4: Final 18 km section from Dumpling Hut to Sandfly Point. Walk through lush rainforest along the Arthur River, passing impressive waterfalls including Bell Rock, Giant Gate Falls, and the Boatshed. The forest becomes increasingly dramatic as you near Milford Sound.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point (~12:30–2:00 PM). Take the water taxi across to Milford Sound (15 min). Celebrate completing the legendary Milford Track! Board an afternoon Milford Sound cruise (1.5–2 hrs, NZD 70–90) — sailing past Mitre Peak and Stirling Falls with views of seals, dolphins, and sheer fiord walls.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer by coach from Milford Sound back to Te Anau (2 hrs, ~5:30 PM arrival). Check back into Te Anau accommodation. Hot shower, laundry, and a well-deserved restaurant dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final self-cooked breakfast on the track at Dumpling Hut
meals.lunch: Pack the last of your trail snacks — eat at Sandfly Point while waiting for the water taxi
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — excellent New Zealand cuisine in a heritage cottage atmosphere, perfect post-track celebration (~NZD 45–60)

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound cruise is strongly recommended and can be booked in advance through Real Journeys or Jucy Cruise. The coach transfer back to Te Anau is included with most track packages or can be booked separately (~NZD 55). Book Te Anau accommodation for this night before starting the track.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Te Anau after the Milford Track. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and do laundry. Take a gentle walk along the Te Anau lakefront or visit the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary (free) to see takahe — one of New Zealand's rarest birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to Queenstown (170 km, ~2 hrs). Stop at the stunning Lake Hayes viewpoint near Arrowtown for photos — one of the most photographed lakes in New Zealand. Check back into the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Queenstown. Browse the night markets (if running) or enjoy a quiet drink at a lakefront bar. Reflect on the incredible week of adventures.

meals.breakfast: Sandfly Café, Te Anau — a local favourite with great eggs benedict and strong coffee (~NZD 18–24)
meals.lunch: Roadside picnic at Lake Hayes — pick up supplies from a Te Anau supermarket before departing
meals.dinner: Pub on Wharf, Queenstown — relaxed waterfront pub with great craft beers and classic New Zealand pub food (~NZD 25–35)

day_by_day.notes: Take the scenic Queenstown-Te Anau highway slowly and stop at Five Rivers and Kingston. The Lake Hayes loop walk (8 km, 2 hrs, flat) is a beautiful option if energy levels allow after the drive. Stock up on groceries in Te Anau before leaving as prices are cheaper than Queenstown.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Wanaka (68 km, ~1 hr from Queenstown via the Crown Range — New Zealand's highest sealed road with spectacular views). Stop at the Crown Range summit lookout for panoramic photos over the Wakatipu Basin. Explore Wanaka township and the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' on the lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Roy's Peak Track (16 km return, 1,200m elevation gain, 5–6 hrs) — one of the most iconic hikes on the South Island with jaw-dropping views over Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring. Start no later than 12:00 PM to allow enough time. Alternatively, if energy is low after the Milford Track, opt for the easier Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain loop (2.5 hrs, moderate).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Queenstown via the Crown Range. Sunset views from the summit are spectacular. Final evening in Queenstown — celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at accommodation before the Crown Range drive
meals.lunch: Pack trail lunch for Roy's Peak — this is essential as there are no facilities on the track
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — upscale but accessible fine dining with incredible lake views, perfect for a final celebration dinner (~NZD 55–75 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a challenging hike — only attempt if legs have recovered from the Milford Track. The summit queue for photos can be long on clear days; start early or be patient. The Crown Range road is steep and winding — drive carefully, especially in wet conditions. Wanaka Beerworks and Pemberton Wines are great afternoon stops if skipping Roy's Peak.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Pack and check out of the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Take one last walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront or up to the Queenstown Hill lookout for a final view. Visit any shops for last-minute New Zealand souvenirs — Merino wool, Manuka honey, and local art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on an incredible 13-day South Island adventure featuring two bungy jumps and two of New Zealand's greatest walks.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street — excellent eggs, pastries, and Queenstown's best coffee (~NZD 20–28)
meals.lunch: Airport café or a final Fergburger to take away before heading to the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport has good shopping and dining options post-security. Allow extra time if checking hiking gear or oversized luggage. Consider purchasing New Zealand Merino wool base layers duty-free — excellent value and a practical souvenir. Confirm flight check-in requirements with your airline, particularly for any bungy jump souvenir items or hiking equipment.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a freefall of 8.5 seconds and is a must-do for adrenaline seekers visiting Queenstown.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing Day Hike
experiences.description: Often ranked as one of the world's best single-day hikes, this 19.4 km trail crosses volcanic terrain, emerald crater lakes, and dramatic lava fields on the South Island's doorstep. Stunning panoramic views reward every step.

experiences.name: Milford Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike the legendary 53.5 km Milford Track through ancient rainforest, past towering waterfalls including Sutherland Falls, and across the MacKinnon Pass. Widely considered the finest walk in the world, this multi-day trek is unforgettable.

experiences.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the plunge at the world's first commercial bungy site, the historic Kawarau Bridge. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River and choose whether to get fully dunked in the water below. A legendary rite of passage in Queenstown.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Day Hike
experiences.description: Explore a section of the world-class Routeburn Track, winding through pristine beech forests, alpine meadows, and alongside crystal-clear mountain streams. The views from Key Summit and Routeburn Falls are absolutely breathtaking and accessible as a day hike.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Check in, settle into your premium accommodation, and enjoy a welcome champagne tour of the property. Take a leisurely stroll around the Nevis Valley landscape to acclimatize and soak in the dramatic gorge scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed first evening at the boutique stay. Enjoy a curated welcome dinner on-site or at a nearby Queenstown restaurant such as Amisfield Winery & Bistro, known for its farm-to-table philosophy and stunning lake views.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — traveling; light snack at Queenstown Airport lounge
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro, Queenstown — multi-course seasonal tasting menu paired with Central Otago wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm check-in time with Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay followed by a guided orientation hike around the Nevis Valley rim trails. Enjoy panoramic views of the Nevis River gorge and surrounding schist rock formations with a private local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a private transfer into central Queenstown (approx. 45 minutes). Visit the Kawarau Bridge Bungy Jump — the world's first commercial bungy site. Leap 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River in a legendary setting. Opt for the private VIP bungy experience with dedicated staff and commemorative footage package.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a celebratory dinner at Rata Restaurant by celebrity chef Josh Emmett — one of Queenstown's finest dining establishments featuring refined New Zealand cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — locally sourced eggs, artisan breads, fresh fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside café lunch at The Bunker or Vudu Café & Larder in Queenstown town centre
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — à la carte fine dining with New Zealand-inspired dishes and premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge VIP Bungy experience in advance through AJ Hackett. Minimum age/weight requirements apply. Wear comfortable, flexible clothing for the jump.

day_by_day.morning: Early start with a private helicopter transfer from Queenstown to the Nevis Bungy platform — the most dramatic way to arrive at New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. Complete your pre-jump briefing with dedicated instructors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the iconic Nevis Bungy Jump — a 8.5-second freefall from the suspended cable car pod. Celebrate post-jump with a private picnic lunch in the Nevis Valley, arranged by the boutique stay, with Central Otago cheeses, charcuterie, and local pinot noir.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a restorative evening. Indulge in an in-room spa treatment (massage or hydrotherapy) booked through the property's concierge, followed by a private chef dinner at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-activity breakfast at the boutique stay — smoothies, granola, and fresh fruit to keep you energized
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic in the Nevis Valley — curated by the boutique stay with local artisan produce and Central Otago wines
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — bespoke 4-course menu using seasonal South Island ingredients

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires advance booking through AJ Hackett. Weight limits apply (45–127 kg). The helicopter transfer option should be confirmed with the concierge at least 48 hours in advance. Weather may affect helicopter access.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the boutique stay. Enjoy a long gourmet breakfast followed by a guided e-bike tour through the Nevis Valley and surrounding high-country farmland. Explore hidden schist gorges and historic gold-mining remnants with a knowledgeable local guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private 4WD high-country tour of the Nevis Road, one of New Zealand's most dramatic backcountry drives. Stop at elevated viewpoints overlooking the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu. Visit a working merino sheep station for a behind-the-scenes farm experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive into Queenstown for dinner. Reserve a table at Botswana Butchery — a premier steakhouse and fine dining restaurant with stunning lakefront views, celebrated for its dry-aged New Zealand beef and outstanding wine cellar.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: High-country picnic basket prepared by the boutique stay, enjoyed at a scenic overlook during the 4WD tour
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — premium dry-aged steaks, South Island lamb, and an extensive New Zealand wine selection

day_by_day.notes: E-bike tour and 4WD high-country experience should be pre-booked through the boutique stay's concierge. Wear layered clothing as high-country temperatures can vary significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private vehicle to Te Anau (approx. 2.5 hours from Queenstown). Check in to a luxury Te Anau lodge such as The Fiordland Lodge. After freshening up, enjoy a morning guided kayak on Lake Te Anau with stunning Fiordland mountain backdrops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a magical underground limestone cave system accessible only by boat. Take a private guided tour for an intimate experience among thousands of glowworms in the cathedral-like cave chambers.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at The Fiordland Lodge's restaurant or a fine dining establishment in Te Anau such as Sandfly Café & Restaurant, known for its locally sourced Fiordland cuisine and relaxed premium atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Nevis Valley Boutique Stay before departure — packed to-go option available for early starters
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at a Te Anau café upon arrival — try Miles Better Pies or a waterfront bistro for a relaxed midday meal
meals.dinner: The Fiordland Lodge restaurant — intimate fine dining featuring local venison, trout, and seasonal Southland produce

day_by_day.notes: This day involves a base change to Te Anau for Milford Track access. Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves private tour through Real Journeys in advance. Fiordland Lodge or equivalent luxury accommodation should be pre-booked.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the legendary Milford Track Great Walk — Day 1 of 4. Depart Te Anau by private boat transfer across Lake Te Anau to the trailhead at Glade Wharf. Begin hiking through ancient podocarp forest along the Clinton River. Arrive at Glade House (private guided walkers hut) — 5 km, gentle terrain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the serene Clinton Valley floor, surrounded by towering beech forest and dramatic valley walls. Spot native birdlife including kea, tomtit, and rifleman. Arrive at Clinton Hut (private guided accommodation) — approximately 16 km total for the day.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the private guided walkers facilities at Clinton Hut. Enjoy a hearty hot dinner prepared by the hut's guided service staff. Share stories with fellow guided walkers around the communal dining area.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Fiordland Lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet trail lunch prepared by Fiordland Lodge — premium sandwiches, energy bars, fruit, and thermos of hot drink
meals.dinner: Hot three-course dinner served at Clinton Hut by Ultimate Hikes guided service staff

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Track must be booked through Ultimate Hikes (guided) for the premium private hut experience. This is a multi-day hike — pack light with only essentials in a day pack as gear transfers are arranged. Waterproof clothing and quality hiking boots are essential. Book well in advance as spots are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 2. Wake to birdsong in the Clinton Valley. After a full guided breakfast, hike from Clinton Hut through the upper Clinton Valley. Pass through stunning alpine meadows and cross numerous swing bridges over glacial streams. Ascend gradually toward Mackinnon Pass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the iconic Mackinnon Pass (1,154 m) — the highest point of the Milford Track — with breathtaking 360-degree views of Fiordland. Celebrate with a packed lunch at the summit shelter. Descend the dramatic western face via the Roaring Burn track, passing the spectacular Sutherland Falls (580 m — one of New Zealand's tallest waterfalls). Arrive at Quintin Lodge.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and dry gear at Quintin Lodge. Hot showers, comfortable private rooms, and a well-earned dinner served by the guided hut team. Optional short evening walk to the base of Sutherland Falls.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Clinton Hut — eggs, bacon, toast, cereals, and hot beverages
meals.lunch: Summit picnic lunch at Mackinnon Pass — packed by guided service with premium trail foods and hot soup thermos
meals.dinner: Three-course hot dinner at Quintin Lodge — hearty New Zealand cuisine featuring local proteins and seasonal vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is the most demanding day of the Milford Track — approximately 14 km with significant elevation gain. Weather at Mackinnon Pass can change rapidly; always carry waterproofs. The detour to Sutherland Falls adds 1 hour return and is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Track Day 3. Final day of hiking. Depart Quintin Lodge and hike through the lower Arthur Valley, passing the beautiful Giant Gate Falls and the dramatic Mackay Falls. The trail winds through lush rainforest draped in moss and ferns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Sandfly Point — the end of the Milford Track — after approximately 18 km of scenic hiking. Board a private boat transfer across Milford Sound to Milford Sound Lodge or the wharf. Celebrate completing one of the world's greatest walks with a glass of champagne.
day_by_day.evening: Board a premium overnight cruise on Milford Sound with Jucy Cruise or Real Journeys' overnight vessel. Enjoy the sound at its most magical — still waters, towering fiord walls, and bioluminescent plankton after dark. Gourmet dinner on board.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at Quintin Lodge before final day's hike
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the final stretch — sandwiches, fruit, snacks, and chocolate
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner on board the Milford Sound overnight cruise — fresh seafood, local meats, and New Zealand wines with fiord views

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Sound overnight cruise must be pre-booked. Real Journeys' Milford Mariner offers premium overnight experiences with private cabins. This is one of the most extraordinary ways to experience Milford Sound — highly recommended as a trip highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up on the Milford Sound overnight cruise to misty fiord scenery. Enjoy a full breakfast on board while the vessel navigates to the Tasman Sea entrance and back through the sound. Watch for dolphins, fur seals, and Fiordland crested penguins from the deck.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Milford Sound wharf. Private luxury vehicle transfer back to Queenstown (approx. 4 hours via the Milford Road — one of New Zealand's most scenic drives). Stop at Mirror Lakes and The Divide for photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Check in to a luxury Queenstown hotel such as The Rees Hotel & Luxury Apartments (lakefront) or Matakauri Lodge. Enjoy a relaxed, celebratory dinner at Kō Restaurant at Matakauri Lodge — arguably Queenstown's most exclusive dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast on board the Milford Sound cruise vessel — hot buffet with eggs, pastries, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Scenic roadside stop lunch at a café in Te Anau during the return drive — or packed premium lunch from the cruise vessel
meals.dinner: Kō Restaurant at Matakauri Lodge — intimate fine dining with panoramic Lake Wakatipu views and a curated New Zealand tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road (SH94) is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow extra time for stops. Book Matakauri Lodge or The Rees Hotel well in advance. This evening marks a transition back to Queenstown luxury base.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the Queenstown luxury hotel. Enjoy a late gourmet breakfast and spa treatment (deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy) to recover from the multi-day hike. Take a gentle lakefront walk along the Queenstown Gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a private guided Routeburn Track Day Hike — explore a curated section of the world-class Routeburn Track winding through pristine beech forest and alpine terrain. A private guide will tailor the route to your fitness level, with highlights including Lake Harris and the Key Summit viewpoint.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a memorable dinner at Fishbone Bar & Grill or The Bunker — Queenstown's celebrated intimate fine dining restaurant known for its exceptional game meats, local fish, and extensive wine list.

meals.breakfast: Extended gourmet breakfast at Matakauri Lodge or The Rees Hotel — eggs your way, smoked salmon, artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Premium packed trail lunch on the Routeburn Track — prepared by the hotel or private guide service with local cheeses, meats, and fruit
meals.dinner: The Bunker Restaurant, Queenstown — cozy fine dining with New Zealand game meats, craft cocktails, and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Private Routeburn Track guided day hike can be arranged through Queenstown-based guiding companies such as Guided Walks NZ. Confirm fitness level with the guide in advance to select the most suitable section of the track.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic helicopter flight from Queenstown over the Remarkables, Mount Aspiring National Park, and the Southern Alps. Land on a remote glacier or alpine snowfield for a champagne morning tea — a quintessential South Island luxury experience arranged through Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown. Spend the afternoon at leisure — browse Queenstown's luxury boutiques on The Mall, visit the Queenstown Arts Centre, or enjoy a wine tasting at a lakefront cellar door. Alternatively, take a private sailing charter on Lake Wakatipu aboard the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro (revisit for a different seasonal menu) or try Rata Restaurant for a final celebration of South Island cuisine. Pair dinner with a flight of Central Otago pinot noir.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before the helicopter flight — fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lakefront lunch at Queenstown's Pier Restaurant or a waterfront bistro — fresh South Island seafood and local produce
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant, Queenstown — seasonal tasting menu with optional wine pairing featuring Central Otago and Marlborough selections

day_by_day.notes: Glacier helicopter experiences are weather-dependent — have a backup plan. Book through Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters or Over The Top Helicopters for premium private charters. TSS Earnslaw private charter must be booked through Real Journeys.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown by private vehicle for Wanaka (approx. 1 hour via Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in New Zealand, with spectacular views). Check in to a luxury Wanaka property such as Minaret Station Alpine Lodge or Edgewater Resort. Morning walk along the Wanaka lakefront to the famous 'That Wanaka Tree.'
day_by_day.afternoon: Guided hike on the Rob Roy Glacier Track in Mount Aspiring National Park (approx. 4 hours return, 10 km). A spectacular trail through ancient beech forest leading to views of the Rob Roy Glacier, hanging glaciers, and alpine waterfalls — one of the South Island's most rewarding day hikes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka for dinner at Ritual Café or Francesca's Italian Kitchen — Wanaka's premier dining destinations. Alternatively, enjoy a private chef dinner at Minaret Station if staying there.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Queenstown hotel before departure — full cooked breakfast with fresh juices and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed premium trail lunch for the Rob Roy Glacier Track — prepared by the lodge with local artisan products
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — intimate fine dining with handmade pasta, local meats, and an exceptional Italian and New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a short drive to the Matukituki Valley from Wanaka (approx. 45 minutes on a gravel road — 4WD recommended). Book a private guide for the best experience. Minaret Station Alpine Lodge offers one of New Zealand's most exclusive wilderness lodge experiences and requires helicopter access.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Wanaka. Enjoy a slow gourmet breakfast at the lodge with views over Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps. Take a final reflective walk along the lakeshore or a gentle hike up Mount Iron (1.5 hours return) for panoramic farewell views of the Wanaka basin.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer back to Queenstown Airport (approx. 1 hour). Depending on departure time, stop at Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved gold-rush era village — for a final browse of artisan boutiques and a farewell coffee at The Chop Shop Food Merchants.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. If flight timing allows, enjoy a final glass of Central Otago pinot noir at the airport lounge or at Winnie's restaurant in central Queenstown before heading to the airport.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at Wanaka lodge — full spread with eggs, local honey, fresh-baked bread, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Arrowtown at Saffron Restaurant — award-winning cuisine in a historic stone building, celebrating Central Otago flavors
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or early dinner at Winnies, Queenstown — depending on flight schedule

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the Queenstown Airport transfer from Wanaka, including any Arrowtown stop. Confirm flight details and arrange private transfer well in advance. Consider purchasing Central Otago pinot noir or Manuka honey as premium souvenirs before departing.

query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026
